alternativas.texto: Data collected with a discovery source of ServiceNow can insert new records into the Windows Server [cmdb_ci_win_server] table, but cannot update records created by Altiris or SCCM.
alternativas.explicacao: The priority numbers assigned to the Discovery Sources indicate the order in which reconciliation rules will be applied. In this case, ServiceNow has the lowest priority, followed by Altiris and then SCCM. This means that data collected from ServiceNow can insert new records into the Windows Server table, but it cannot update records created by higher-priority sources like Altiris or SCCM.

alternativas.texto: Data collected with a discovery source of Altiris can update records inserted by SCCM into the Windows Server [cmdb_ci_win_server] table.
alternativas.explicacao: Since Altiris has a higher priority than SCCM, data collected with a discovery source of Altiris can update records inserted by SCCM into the Windows Server table. The reconciliation rules prioritize the updates based on the order of the Discovery Sources' priority numbers.

alternativas.texto: Data collected with a discovery source of SCCM can update any record in the Windows Server [cmdb_ci_win_server] table because it has the highest priority number
alternativas.explicacao: While SCCM has the highest priority number among the Discovery Sources, it does not mean that it can update any record in the Windows Server table. The priority numbers determine the order in which reconciliation rules are applied, but they do not grant unlimited update access. SCCM can only update records that it has inserted or that have a lower priority source.

alternativas.texto: Data collected with a discovery source of SCCM can be inserted as new records in Windows Server [cmdb_ci_win_sever] table
alternativas.explicacao: The priority number assigned to SCCM is the highest among the Discovery Sources listed. pergunta: A CMDB Administrator has a report in ServiceNow that lists all CMDB Services that do not have an owner and wants to use a ServiceNow Playbook.What Governance process play can prevent this from recurring?

alternativas.texto: Make the field Managed by mandatory on all CIs
alternativas.explicacao: Making the field Managed by mandatory on all Configuration Items (CIs) may help in ensuring that all CIs have a designated manager, but it does not directly address the issue of services not having an owner. This governance process play may not prevent the recurrence of services without an owner in the CMDB report.

alternativas.texto: Make the field Owned by mandatory
alternativas.explicacao: Making the field Owned by mandatory ensures that all CMDB Services have an owner assigned to them. By enforcing this requirement, the CMDB Administrator can prevent the occurrence of services without an owner in the report. This governance process play directly addresses the issue at hand and helps maintain data integrity in the CMDB.

alternativas.texto: Set a default value on the Service Owner field so that is never empty
alternativas.explicacao: Setting a default value on the Service Owner field may help in pre-populating the field with a value, but it does not guarantee that the field will always have a valid owner assigned. This approach may not be as effective as making the field Owned by mandatory, as it does not enforce the requirement of having a designated owner for each CMDB Service.

pergunta: The CMDB Administrator wants to leverage the Staleness metric from the CMDB Health Dashboard - Correctness Scorecard.Which field is used to calculate the duration of this metric?

alternativas.explicacao: The "Last modified on" field (last_modified) indicates the last time a record was modified in the CMDB. While this information is important for tracking changes, it is not directly used to calculate the duration of the Staleness metric in the CMDB Health Dashboard.

The "Updated" field (sys_updated_on) is used to track the last time a record was updated or modified in the CMDB. This field is crucial for calculating the duration of the Staleness metric, as it helps determine how long it has been since the record was last updated.

The "Created" field (sys_created_on) represents the date and time when a record was initially created in the CMDB. This information is not relevant for calculating the duration of the Staleness metric, as it does not reflect the most recent update or change to the record.

The "First discovered" field (first_discovered) indicates the initial discovery date of a record in the CMDB. While this information is valuable for understanding the history of a record, it is not directly utilized in calculating the duration of the Staleness metric in the CMDB Health Dashboard.

The "Most recent discovery" field (last_discovery) shows the date and time of the most recent discovery of a record in the CMDB. While this information is important for tracking the latest discovery event, it is not specifically used to calculate the duration of the Staleness metric in the CMDB Health Dashboard.

pergunta: A CMDB Administrator wants to ensure that only relevant CIs from managed classes will be shown on Incident, Problem, and Change records.Which checkbox needs to be checked in the CI Class Manager for the CMDB Administrator to achieve the requested result?

alternativas.explicacao: The "Extensible" checkbox in the CI Class Manager allows for the class to be extended with additional attributes and relationships. While this setting can be useful for customization, it does not control the visibility of CIs on Incident, Problem, and Change records.

The "Independent" checkbox in the CI Class Manager does not directly relate to the visibility of CIs on Incident, Problem, and Change records. This setting is more about defining whether a class can exist independently or needs to be associated with another class.

The "Main Record" checkbox in the CI Class Manager is used to designate a class as the main record for a configuration item. It does not control which CIs are shown on Incident, Problem, and Change records. This setting is more about defining the primary record for a CI rather than controlling visibility in other records.

By checking the "Principal Class" checkbox in the CI Class Manager, the CMDB Administrator ensures that only relevant CIs from managed classes will be shown on Incident, Problem, and Change records. This setting restricts the visibility of CIs to only those that are directly related to the records, helping to maintain data integrity and relevance in the CMDB.

pergunta: A Configuration Management Governance team is transitioning from utilizing legacy CMDB status fields to CSDM life cycle status fields.Which table can be modified?

This table is used to track the status of items as they progress through the defined life cycle stages.

The Life Cycle Stages [life_cycle_stage] table typically contains predefined stages in the CSDM life cycle model and is not meant to be modified by users. It is used to define the standard stages of an item's life cycle and is not directly related to transitioning from legacy CMDB status fields to CSDM life cycle status fields.

The Life Cycle Controls [life_cycle_control] table typically contains configurations related to controlling the life cycle of items in the CSDM model. It is not directly related to transitioning from legacy CMDB status fields to CSDM life cycle status fields and is not meant to be modified for this purpose.

The Life Cycle Mapping [life_cycle_mapping] table is the table that can be modified to transition from legacy CMDB status fields to CSDM life cycle status fields. pergunta: A Configuration Manager wants to use the Unified Map.Where would it be accessed?

alternativas.explicacao: The CMDB Data Manager is responsible for managing the data within the CMDB, such as importing, exporting, and updating CI data. While it plays a crucial role in maintaining the integrity of the CMDB, it does not provide access to the Unified Map feature, which is specifically designed for visualizing CI relationships.

The CMDB Workspace is the correct location to access the Unified Map feature. The Unified Map allows Configuration Managers to visualize the relationships and dependencies between CIs within the CMDB in a graphical format. This feature provides a visual representation of the CI relationships, making it easier to understand the impact of changes and analyze the configuration data.

The CI Class Manager is responsible for managing Configuration Item (CI) classes and their attributes within the CMDB. It does not provide access to the Unified Map feature, as its primary function is related to CI class management.

pergunta: A customer wants to model their business applications and would like to capture different types of data that includes Personally Identifiable Information (PII) data.Based on these requirements, which CMDB class needs to be leveraged to achieve this?

It allows for the classification, organization, and management of data within the CMDB, making it the appropriate choice for the customer's requirements.

The API Component CMDB class is used to represent the components of an API, such as endpoints, methods, and parameters. It is not intended for capturing and managing data, including Personally Identifiable Information (PII) data.

The Business Capability CMDB class is used to model the high-level capabilities of a business, such as processes, functions, and services. It is not specifically designed to capture and manage data, including Personally Identifiable Information (PII) data.

The Data Classification CMDB class is used to classify and categorize data based on its sensitivity, importance, and regulatory requirements. While important for data governance, it does not directly capture and manage data, including Personally Identifiable Information (PII) data, as the Information Object class does.

The Compliance scorecard in the CMDB Health Dashboard focuses on ensuring that the data in the CMDB aligns with defined policies, standards, and regulations. The Completeness scorecard in the CMDB Health Dashboard is designed to track the completeness of data for CIs and CI classes. pergunta: When integrating data into the CMDB using import sets and transform maps, which type of script is added to ensure the data is processed through the IRE?

This script allows for data manipulation and validation before the actual import process takes place, making it a crucial step in the integration process.

The `onStart` script is executed at the beginning of the integration process, but it does not specifically ensure that the data is processed through the IRE. It is more focused on initializing variables or performing actions before the data processing begins.

The `onAfter` script is typically used to perform actions after the data has been imported into the CMDB. While it can be used for post-processing tasks, it does not ensure that the data is processed through the IRE during the integration process.

The `onComplete` script is typically used to perform actions after the import set has been processed and the data has been imported into the CMDB. It does not specifically ensure that the data is processed through the IRE during the integration process.
